_about: Chapter R (Resolve) of the suite results document, round 2 (after OWNER-REVIEW-SAMPLE-1.md): the prose data of DESIGN-DOC.md section 5 for manifest v4 (units as in units_v4.json). `summary` (what held, and the timing in one paragraph) and `coverage_gap` (which claim remains unsupported) are printed first on the chapter page, before and after the summary block (standing, outcomes, agreement, timing, load, detail blocks), in this run's figures (re-read them for every release; the family prose holds run facts too). `intro` follows: the shortened /resolve background. `families` keys on the family id (the scenario id prefix) with a title and one paragraph; `units` keys on the unit id with its one-line property, a string or {property, note} (the note printed in italics under the property line). `mcp_notes.units` keys on a unit id whose MCP column is wholly not exercised: the one line printed under its table (the per-case reasons are in cases.json). Keys are family and unit ids, never scenario ids. Inline markup: `code` and *emphasis*. Chapter placeholders: {n_tests}, {n_units}, {n_families}, {n_detail} and the overview's. Every claim follows SPEC-labeled-traversal-core.md section 4, areas.py gen_R, checks.py and service_by_design.json as of c11db9dd; recorded facts are the v4 run's (20261014T061053Z, re-evaluated with c11db9dd). The check catalogue is in checks.json, the glossary in glossary.json.
title: Resolve
summary: *What held.* On the direct arms every property this chapter asks of /resolve held wherever the host answered: 76 of the 81 tests pass on direct-local and 78 on direct-remote, with no failure, no error and no disagreement between arms (79 identical pairs, 2 differing by a time limitation alone). The window of a record resolves fully under its taxid column and its header at every length from one k-mer to 2,000 bp (R-pos, 27 of 28), labels in one request are answered independently of each other and of their order (R-multi, R-order), a junction's runs end where the records say (R-junction), a discovery lists the source or states a truncation that SPEC section 4.2 allows (R-discover), support trace gives one contiguous run (R-trace), a reverse complement is another query on this forward-strand graph (R-rc), every refusal carries the host's exact text and every accepted edge the right profile (R-edge), the budget above the cap is lowered and stated and the budget at the reserve refused (R-edge-0021, -0020), and no 200 ever exceeded its budget. Via MCP 51 pairs agree, all fully checked, and the 14 by-design pairs matched the service's table; 16 tests could not be exercised through the tools (a known limit: support trace, the 10 kb resolves, seven edge inputs; I.4 and appendix B).

*Timing.* Host-warm, a resolve of up to 2,000 bp answers in milliseconds on the direct arms (server p50 3 ms; wall p50 4 ms on direct-local, 13 ms on direct-remote) and in 0.6 s at the median via MCP, of which the host call is 74 ms and the rest the service's submit, queue, terminal lag and paging; the host-cold direct-local calls (n 29) reach 11 s at p90, the 10 kb resolves and the trace resolves among them. The record matters more than the length: the two 2,000 bp windows differ by two orders of magnitude on the same arm and state (hvo within 0.2 s, pfa in seconds or a 503), because the work is the rows of the window's k-mers (section 4.1), not its bases. Every figure was taken under the Logan load (I.4).
coverage_gap: *What remains unsupported.* The stated stop of SPEC section 4.5, a 200 that answers exactly the resolve of a prefix with a stop block, was not exercised successfully in this run: neither 10 kb stop (R-budget-0001 under 3,000 ms, R-budget-0002 under 8,000 ms) nor the full 20 s twins produced one. On this host under the Logan load they answered 503 deadline (allowed, inconclusive) or, four times, a 503 delivered more than max(1 s, the budget) after the budget: 6.1 s and 7.5 s late on the two arms of R-budget-0001, 9.5 s late on direct-remote for R-budget-0002 and 25.5 s late for R-twin-0002 eco, the chapter's and the run's only findings (SPEC section 4.5 names the pieces its deadline does not poll: the query's k-mer mapping and one row batch). So the prefix property and three of the four `prefix_equals` relations are inconclusive on every arm (`REL-prefix_equals-0004` passes on direct-remote, where pae's full twin completed in 0.4 s host-warm), and the claim that a stop answers the prefix rests on no evidence from this host; the v4 gate's declared file excludes the three relations on direct-local for those reasons, and the five tests sit in the detail blocks of R-budget. The 2,000 bp window of pfa (R-pos-0027) is the other inconclusive: a 503 deadline at 24 s on direct-local (allowed under a budget) and the service's backend deadline on the cold MCP call (a host state), with direct-remote and the warm MCP call passing. Each of these blocks the deploy gate on a gated arm (I.1).
intro: POST /resolve maps a query to the labels that carry it (SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 4). For a query of L bases the host maps its L - k + 1 k-mers to the graph (on this basic graph the forward strand only) and reports `graph_runs`, the maximal runs of consecutive in-graph k-mers as 0-based half-open intervals of k-mer starts, and per requested label the k-mers it supports, as runs of the same form and as a count, `kmers_supported`. A column label (a taxid) supports an in-graph k-mer whose annotation row carries it; a header label (an accession.version) one at which some coordinate of its column maps to that sequence, and with support trace only while consecutive supported k-mers have consecutive coordinates (section 4.2). A request names exactly one of labels or discover; a discovery collects the labels of every in-graph k-mer's row, ranks them by supported k-mers, keeps the top `max_labels` (ties by column id, then sequence id) and states `labels_truncated` when it dropped some. Validation is strict: an unknown field, a wrong type, a value out of range, both or neither of labels and discover, a duplicate or unknown label, a query shorter than k or longer than the server's or the request's `max_query_bp` are 400s naming the problem. The select block (section 4.3) is not exercised by this chapter.

The time budget (section 4.5) is opt-in: `bounds.time_budget_ms`, above the finalisation reserve of 250 ms, lowered to the server's cap (60,000 ms on staging) and stated in limits.clamped when lowered. The work reads the deadline between its row batches and its pieces of k-mers and stops at the budget less the reserve; a stop answers, with status 200, exactly the resolve of a prefix of the query with a stop block (phase, reason time, `resolved_kmers`, `query_kmers`, `resolved_bp`, `remainder_from_bp`), so that a client resolves the rest from `remainder_from_bp`. Past the budget the answer is a 503 with the code deadline, never a partial answer. The pieces the deadline does not poll (the request's parse, the mapping of the query's k-mers, one row batch's decode, the explicit labels' resolution) can push a stop or a 503 past the budget; a 503 deadline is allowed, and inconclusive, wherever the request names a budget, and a finding only beyond max(1 s, the budget) (appendix A, `budget_respected`).

Ground truth. The windows are cut from the records of I.2; the record's taxid column and its accession.version are the labels, and every k-mer of a window cut from the record is in the graph and supported by both. Lengths run from k to 2,000 bp, the cap the service sends on every explicit-label resolve; the 10 kb stops of R-budget run up to the server's limit of 10,000 bp and reach the host on the direct arms only. R-pos, R-multi, R-junction, R-trace, R-rc, R-order, R-twin-case and most of R-edge name `bounds.time_budget_ms` 20,000 and `bounds.max_query_bp` 2,000 on every explicit-label request, as the service sends them, so that the direct arms and the MCP arm ask the same question; a discovery names `max_query_bp` 500 and no budget. The scenarios that vary a bound on purpose: the two stops of R-budget (3,000 and 8,000 ms, no request bound), their 10 kb twins R-twin-0002 to -0005 and the 10,001 bp edge R-edge-0003 (the 20,000 ms budget alone), R-edge-0004 (a request bound of 100 bp), R-edge-0012 (no bounds) and the budget edges R-edge-0020, -0021 and -0024 (250, 70,000 and 400 ms).

Via MCP a resolve is the `traverse_resolve` tool, a job the service runs in its queue (case `resolve.job_path`): the tool waits inline up to 30 s with explicit labels and 10 s for a discovery, else hands back a job the runner polls; the service's own deadline for the host call is the budget plus the reserve plus an allowance of 10,000 ms (30.25 s here), and a call it ends there is a `resolve_timeout`, read as a host state when the service's timing shows the deadline was reached. The service validates first and in its own terms: it always sends its own `bounds.max_query_bp` (2,000; 500 for a discovery) and refuses a longer query at submit, so the 10 kb scenarios cannot be expressed; it de-duplicates labels, upper-cases the sequence, and refuses any character outside ACGT, more than 1,000 distinct labels, a budget below 500 ms or above the host's cap, and a discovery limit outside 1..100; support, select and graph have no argument. The MCP column therefore holds many by-design and not-exercised cells; each carries its reason in one line, and appendix B names every case with the service's code and text.

R-pos.title: positive windows
R-pos.prose: Windows of 31, 32, 50, 100, 200, 1,000 and 2,000 bp cut from the records, resolved under the record's own taxid column and under its header label. The property is the simplest claim /resolve makes and the ground every other chapter stands on: every k-mer of a window taken from a record is in the graph and supported by that record's labels, as one run covering the whole query (`resolve_runs`, full), and `graph_runs` is that same single run (`resolve_graph_runs`). The lengths bracket the k-mer count from one (31 bp) and two (32 bp) to 1,970 (2,000 bp, the cap the service sends). The series changes the source record with the length, two records per length (A: eco 31, mtb 32, pae 50, cje 100, mge 200, ser 1,000, hvo 2,000 bp; B: buc, mpn, mja, sso, spo, scem, pfa in the same order), so the matrices are correctness controls across lengths and records, not a runtime-versus-length benchmark: a cell's time is the record's rows as much as the window's bases, and the 2,000 bp cells of the A and B matrices (hvo, pfa) differ by orders of magnitude for that reason. Each request names the 20,000 ms budget, so a 503 deadline is allowed under load and reads inconclusive; the one such case of this run, the 2,000 bp window of pfa on direct-local (a 503 at 24 s) and on the cold MCP call (the service's `resolve_timeout`), sits in the detail block of its unit; direct-remote (8.2 s) and the warm MCP call (6.1 s) passed. The four units are the column and header halves over the two record sets.

R-multi.title: several labels
R-multi.prose: One 100 bp window per scenario resolved under three labels at once: the record's taxid column, its header, and the taxid column of a record from another kingdom. The record's two labels must support every k-mer (`resolve_runs`, full, once per label); the unrelated column must not support all of them (`label_not_full`). The second claim rests on the assumption that a random, DUST-filtered 100 bp window of one kingdom has at least one k-mer that a genome of another kingdom lacks; a window from a gene conserved across kingdoms would break it, and the truth of each scenario states so. Together with R-order this is the evidence that labels in one request are answered independently of each other.

R-junction.title: junctions
R-junction.prose: The concatenation of two 100 bp windows from records of different kingdoms, resolved under both taxid columns. The expected runs are computed from the records, not assumed: A's column has the run [0, `a_end`), where `a_end` is 70 plus the number of B's leading bases that happen to repeat A's own continuation in its record (at most k - 1), and B's column has [`b_start`, 170), where `b_start` is 100 less the number of A's trailing bases that repeat what precedes B's window in its record. `resolve_runs` asks for exactly these runs, so a label whose run reaches into the other record's k-mers is a wrong answer. A junction k-mer that another record of the same column happens to hold would move a run end; the builder does not model that, and the four junctions of this run end at 70, 70, 71 and 76 for A and start at 98, 99, 100 and 100 for B.

R-discover.title: discovery
R-discover.prose: A 100 bp window from a record with few relatives in RefSeq (a low-carrier genome: buc, mge, mpn, ser, mja, sso) resolved without labels, discovering column labels or header labels with `max_labels` 1, 20 or 100 (`bounds.max_query_bp` 500 and no time budget, as the service sends a discovery; a discovery reads every in-graph k-mer's whole row). The property (`resolve_discover_contains`) is that the source record's own label, its taxid column or its accession.version, is listed. The source supports every in-graph k-mer of the query, so a truncated list may leave it out only in a tie at that full support, which the check verifies from `labels_truncated` (the least support kept and the most support dropped both equal to the in-graph k-mer count, at least one dropped label at full length), the ranking being all the answer can show: the tie is decided by column id, then sequence id, which the answer does not state. The invariants also require the list ranked by support, at most `max_labels` long and `labels_truncated` consistent with it. With `max_labels` 1 the source is regularly outranked in a tie (R-discover-0001 of this run: kept 1 of 9 labels; it and 7 of the 8 dropped labels support all 70 k-mers); that passes, as SPEC section 4.2's tie rule says.

R-trace.title: trace support
R-trace.prose: 200 bp of a record resolved under its header with support trace: beyond presence, consecutive supported k-mers must have consecutive coordinates in that sequence (SPEC section 4.2), so a window cut from the record is exactly one contiguous run over every k-mer (`resolve_runs`, full). The three records, E. coli, S. aureus and phage lambda, differ in the size of their column and in the number of records it holds. Not exercised via MCP: the `traverse_resolve` tool has no support argument (see B); the direct executions are host-cold for that reason (no MCP call reached the host before them) and the aggregate says so.

R-budget.title: the time budget
R-budget.prose: 10 kb of a record (E. coli under 3,000 ms, P. aeruginosa under 8,000 ms; windows drawn without the uniqueness requirement and with the DUST threshold raised to 5) under a budget chosen so that the work stops inside the query on a cold or loaded host and completes on a warm one. The property is the stated stop of SPEC section 4.5: the answer is the resolve of a prefix, its stop block consistent (`num_kmers` equal to `resolved_kmers`, `resolved_bp` and `remainder_from_bp` derived from it, the stop at or after the budget less the reserve), and the record's own label supports every k-mer of that prefix as one run (`resolve_runs`, full with `prefix_if_stopped`). A complete answer never exercised the property and reads inconclusive; a 503 deadline is allowed and reads inconclusive, or a finding when it comes more than max(1 s, the budget) late (`budget_respected`). The two twins of each stop, the same 10 kb under 20,000 ms (R-twin-0002 and -0004, full unless stopped) and its second half from base 5,000 (R-twin-0003 and -0005), are what the `prefix_equals` relations compare the stop against: on their common k-mers the graph runs and the label's runs must be the same sets. In this run, on this host under the Logan load, the two stops and the full 20 s twin of eco answered 503 on both direct arms, between 1 and 25 s past their budgets (findings where more than max(1 s, the budget) late: the query's k-mer mapping and one row batch are not polled), and the full twin of pae answered 503 on direct-local and completed on direct-remote in 0.4 s (host-warm, after the interrupted direct-local call). The stated stop has not been observed on this host, so the prefix property reads inconclusive wherever it was asked. Of the four relations, all four read inconclusive on direct-local and via MCP (no two profiles to compare); on direct-remote three do and `REL-prefix_equals-0004` passes, pae's continuation agreeing with its completed full twin on the k-mers 5,000 to 9,970. The v4 deploy gate's declared file excludes `REL-prefix_equals-0001` and -0003 on direct-local because the stated stop was never testable there, and -0002 because eco's full 10 kb never completed on this host, so that the profile its continuation is compared against does not exist. Not exercised via MCP: the query exceeds the service's supported length of 2,000 bp, so every call was refused at submit (see B).

R-edge.title: edge inputs
R-edge.prose: The edges of /resolve's validation and of its alphabet, one input each, on 100 bp of E. coli unless the edge is the length (the two discovery edges, R-edge-0022 and -0023, take its first 60 bp). Refused inputs expect the host's exact 400 text, or its prefix where the text carries a value: k - 1 bases, 10,001 bp (above the server's limit of 10,000), 200 bp against a request bound of 100, an unknown label (named), a duplicate label (refused, not merged, as the source decides), an empty sequence, discover together with labels and neither of the two, an unknown field (named), graph and graphs on a single-graph server, a body that is not an object and one that is not JSON, a budget not above the 250 ms reserve, and `discover.max_labels` 0. Accepted inputs expect a 200 with the right profile: exactly k bases (one k-mer, `graph_runs` [[0, 1]]); an N or an IUPAC R at position 50, which /resolve does not refuse, the 31 k-mers holding it being absent from the graph (`graph_runs` [[0, 20], [51, 70]]) and the label supporting the 39 others; lower case, resolved as upper case; 1,001 explicit labels, which the host does not cap; a random 200 bp with no k-mer in the graph (`resolve_absent`); a budget of 70,000 ms lowered to the server's 60,000 and stated (clamped); and the two split cases the service refuses but the host answers, `discover.max_labels` 150 and a budget of 400 ms. The texts of the refusals were read from the source where no smoke run had exercised them (tag code-derived). The expectation column is the host's; via MCP most of the family is decided by the service, in four ways the tables state per row with the service's status and code: not expressible through MCP (seven inputs: a request bound other than the service's, the 10,001 bp query the service refuses at its own 2,000 before the host's limit applies, an unknown field, graph, graphs, the two protocol bodies); refused before host execution (eleven inputs the service's own validation or its route refuses at submit); the host's refusal relayed through the service under its own code (two: k - 1 bases, the unknown label); and answered after service normalisation (the duplicate labels of R-edge-0009, de-duplicated, so the host answers 200 where the direct request is refused; the lower case of R-edge-0007, upper-cased, where the answers agree). Each such pair is a by-design case that appendix B names and the comparison verified.

R-rc.title: reverse complement
R-rc.prose: The reverse complement of a 100 bp window that occurs once on either strand of its record (S. aureus, M. jannaschii), resolved under the record's header. On this basic graph a k-mer and its reverse complement are different nodes and the index holds the records' forward strands, so the header supports none of the query's k-mers: `kmers_supported` 0, the label still listed (`resolve_runs` with kmers 0). The k-mers may or may not be in the graph through other genomes; the check does not ask. This is the resolve-side statement of the strand fact that chapters P, T and N test on their routes.

R-order.title: label order
R-order.prose: The labels of an R-multi request in another order (header, unrelated column, taxid) on a 100 bp window of H. volcanii: the taxid column and the header support every k-mer as when they are named first. `resolve_runs` reads a label by its name, so the check is order-blind by construction; the scenario tests that the host is too.

R-twin.title: twins
R-twin.prose: The upper-case twin of the lower-case resolve R-edge-0007: the same 100 bp of E. coli in upper case, expected full under the column, and the relation `same_answer`, which requires the two bodies to be equal apart from timing, on every arm (via MCP the service upper-cases the lower-case request before the host sees it, so the two answers are the same there too). The other twins made for relations, the full and the continued 10 kb resolves, are printed with R-budget, whose relations they serve.

R-pos-column-A.property: A window cut from the record resolves fully under the record's taxid column: every k-mer supported, one run [0, L - k + 1), `graph_runs` the same run.
R-pos-column-A.note: The columns vary the window length and the source record together (eco, mtb, pae, cje, mge, ser, hvo): correctness controls across lengths and records, not a runtime-versus-length benchmark (a cell's time is the record's rows as much as the window's bases).

units.R-pos-column-B: The same property on the second record of each length (buc, mpn, mja, sso, spo, scem, pfa).

R-pos-header-A.property: A window cut from the record resolves fully under the record's header label (accession.version): every k-mer supported, one run [0, L - k + 1), `graph_runs` the same run.
R-pos-header-A.note: The columns vary the window length and the source record together (eco, mtb, pae, cje, mge, ser, hvo): correctness controls across lengths and records, not a runtime-versus-length benchmark (a cell's time is the record's rows as much as the window's bases).

units.R-pos-header-B: The same property on the second record of each length (buc, mpn, mja, sso, spo, scem, pfa).
units.R-multi: Three labels in one request: the record's taxid column and its header support every k-mer (one run each); the other kingdom's column does not support all of them.
units.R-junction: Two 100 bp windows of different kingdoms concatenated: A's column has exactly the run [0, `a_end`) and B's exactly [`b_start`, 170), both ends computed from the records' own continuations.
units.R-discover: A discovery without labels lists the source record's label (column or header) within `max_labels`, or states a truncation that can hide it only in a tie at full support.
units.R-trace: support trace on 200 bp of the record under its own header: one contiguous run over every k-mer, the coordinates consecutive throughout.
units.R-budget: A 10 kb resolve under a small budget stops with a stated prefix the record's label fully supports, or answers 503 deadline (allowed: inconclusive); its twins, the full 20 s resolve and the continuation from base 5,000, agree with it on their common k-mers (relations `prefix_equals`).
units.R-edge-refused: A malformed or out-of-bound request is refused with 400 and the exact text (or prefix) the host's source states, before any work; the expectation is the host's, the MCP cell says how the service answered.
units.R-edge-accepted: An edge input the host accepts is answered with the right profile: exactly k bases; an N or IUPAC code (its 31 k-mers absent, the rest supported); lower case; 1,001 labels; an absent random sequence; a budget above the cap lowered and stated; and the two values the service refuses but the host answers.
units.R-rc: The reverse complement of a window unique on both strands: on this basic, forward-strand graph the record's header supports none of its k-mers (`kmers_supported` 0).
units.R-order: The same labels in another order are each answered as if named alone.
units.R-twin-case: The lower-case resolve (R-edge-0007) and its upper-case twin answer byte for byte alike, timing aside (relation `same_answer`).

units.R-trace: Not exercised via MCP: the `traverse_resolve` tool has no support argument; see B.
units.R-budget: Not exercised via MCP: the 10 kb query exceeds the service's supported length of 2,000 bp, and the tool cannot send another `bounds.max_query_bp`; every call was refused at submit (`resolve_query_too_long`); see B.
